title: Gather Tokens With Free Double Steps
statement:
Tokens sit on a number line. spots[i] is the position of token i; several tokens may share a position.

You may move any token as often as you like. Moving it 2 steps left or right is free. Moving it 1 step left or right costs 1.

Return the smallest total cost to bring every token to one common position.

examples.why: 4, 6 and 12 are even and can meet for free. Only the 9 has to pay one step to switch to an even position.
Three tokens are odd and two are even. Bring everything to an odd spot: only the two even tokens pay.
Distance does not matter, only parity. Two tokens are even, one is odd.

hints: What does a free 2-step move preserve about a position?
Free moves never change whether a position is even or odd, and inside one parity class every token can reach every other spot for free.
So all even tokens can gather for free, and all odd ones too. One group then pays 1 per token to switch parity. Pick the smaller group.

explain.intuition:
A 2-step move keeps the parity of a position. So, at no cost, every even token can reach any even position and every odd token any odd position. Distance is irrelevant.

The only thing that ever costs money is changing parity, and each token needs at most one paid step to do it. If everyone meets on an even spot, each odd token pays 1. If everyone meets on an odd spot, each even token pays 1. Take the cheaper option: min(evens, odds).
steps: Count tokens at even positions and at odd positions.
Return the smaller of the two counts.
pitfalls: Picking the median position and summing distances, as in the usual meeting-point problem. Here distance is free.
Thinking a token far away pays more. One paid step is enough to change parity; the rest is free.
Counting distinct positions instead of tokens. Three tokens stacked on one odd spot still pay 3.

solutions.title: Try every target position
solutions.idea: For each token's position as the meeting point, each other token pays 1 if its parity differs. Keep the minimum.

solutions.title: Count parities
solutions.idea: Gathering within a parity class is free, so only the smaller class pays, 1 per token.

followups: Free moves are 3 steps instead of 2. How does the answer change?
A 1-step move costs a different amount for each token. What do you compute then?
lcTitle: Minimum Cost to Move Chips to The Same Position
